judge_assessment.explanation: The numbers are right and I confirm each: the warm-up vector is (4-(-3), -1-2) = (7,-3); Lee's corrected vector is (-3-2, 1-5) = (-5,-4); AB = 5 while Kim's A'B' = sqrt(16+16) = 5.66, so the corrected B'_y is 5 + (-1) = 4; OP = 5 and OP' = 15 give k = 3; and Ravi's correct image is (2+2(5-2), 1+2(3-1)) = (8,5) with CA' = sqrt(36+16) = 7.21. But this is the clearest failure of open-response labelling in my batch, and the judge recorded one manual item and moved on. The whole instructional mode is misconception analysis, and four problems besides the flagged one require written diagnosis: problem 2 ("Explain what that does to a vector"), problem 3(c) ("what do your two answers prove about Kim's work?"), problem 4(c) ("say in one sentence why a difference can never be a scale factor") and problem 5(a) ("Which centre did his method actually use?", whose answer is the word "the origin", not a number). verify.json carries a single `manual` entry, for problem 6, and final_response.md states "Problem 6 only". The prompt explicitly required that genuinely open responses be clearly labelled for manual review, so this is prompt adherence as well as verification coverage.

strengths_to_preserve: The trap library is the richest in the batch - ten declared traps across five problems, each binding a specific wrong VALUE to a named misconception: -7 and 3 for the reversed subtraction, 5 for applying only the horizontal component, 6 and 10 for difference-instead-of-ratio scale factors, and 9.43 for measuring from the origin instead of from the centre C(2,1).

Problem 3 is built so the diagnosis is forced by arithmetic rather than asserted: AB = 5 against Kim's A'B' = 5.66 makes the rigid-motion violation visible before the student is asked to name it, and the corrected y-coordinate 4 is a separate verified entry.

The two-decimal-place instruction in the directions is matched by "tol": 0.01 on exactly the two entries whose answers are irrational (5.66 and 7.21), so the rounding the sheet asks for is the rounding the verifier accepts.

Problem 6's manual descriptor states the full-credit argument (the images are congruent but differently placed because each point moves along the ray from ITS OWN centre; the centre is recovered as the intersection of two point-to-image lines, being the one fixed point), which is a usable rubric rather than a restatement of the question.

root_causes.description: In a misconception-analysis sheet the diagnosis IS the deliverable, but only problems whose entire response is prose were given `manual` entries. Wherever an explanation shared a problem with a checkable number, the number was declared and the explanation was not.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 2 asks the student to "Explain what that does to a vector" before writing the vector; verify.json id 2 holds two `eval` entries and no `manual`.

Problem 3(c) ("what do your two answers prove about Kim's work?"), problem 4(c) ("say in one sentence why a difference can never be a scale factor") and problem 5(a) ("Which centre did his method actually use?") are all prose responses with no `manual` entry.
verify.json contains exactly one `manual` entry (problem 6) and final_response.md line 38 reports "Problem 6 only".
The prompt requires: "clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review".

root_causes.description: Problems 3, 4 and 5 each ask for three lettered responses and print one auto-emitted answer blank, so there is no place to record the individual parts the key and the verify entries distinguish.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 5 asks (a) which centre, (b) the corrected x- and y-coordinates, (c) CA' to two decimals - four responses - and prints a single "Answer: ____".
answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row 5 is "8, 5, 7.21", three numbers against one blank.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problems 2, 3(c), 4(c) and 5(a) must each gain a `manual` entry; problem 6's existing descriptor is the template to copy.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

improvements.title: One answer blank per requested value - no lumped blank, no orphan blank
improvements.proposed_change: SKILL.md's "Answer location (every problem gets one)" should read "every REQUESTED VALUE gets one": a multi-part problem ends each part with its own \ansline/\answerline inside the stem (which already suppresses \problem's automatic blank, as the preamble documents), and no problem emits a trailing unlabelled blank once every part already has one. Extend tests/check_answer_line.py, which today only binds units, to compare answer-location macros against the distinct non-manual verify entries for the problem id and fail in both directions. Here problems 3, 4 and 5 need one blank per lettered part instead of a single trailing line.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture pair for tests/check_answer_line.py: (a) a problem printing one \ansline against four verify entries must exit non-zero, and (b) the same problem with one \ansline per part must exit 0; plus (c) a problem whose parts all carry blanks and which then emits a trailing \ansline must exit non-zero. All three pass today because the checker never counts blanks.
improvements.expected_impact: The student knows where each requested value goes and the grader can map a Quick Answers row onto the sheet position by position.
improvements.risk: Per-part blanks consume vertical space, so a few dense sheets will gain a page; the gate must also allow a deliberate \noansline on sketch/proof items.

case_summary: Mathematically exact and pedagogically sharp: six problems that isolate the wrong-order vector, the partial vector, the difference-as-scale-factor and the wrong-centre errors, with ten declared traps and tolerances that match the rounding the sheet requests. The failure is one of labelling: this is a diagnosis sheet in which four of the six problems demand a written diagnosis, and only the last one is flagged for manual review, so the packet reports far more machine coverage than it actually has and the prompt's explicit labelling instruction is only partly met.
